data.body:
Read-only investigation complete. Root cause confirmed, and the severity is higher than "operational toil": this is a signing-correctness hole, not just a stale checkout.

## Root cause

The MCP code workspace (`gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`) is a persistent `main` checkout that is cloned once and thereafter only reused. No deployed path advances its working-tree HEAD. Autodeploy advances a *separate* mirror and its own deploy marker files, never this volume.

`infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` defines "present" as `.git` exists plus HEAD resolves, with no freshness check at all:

- `:12` `MCP_CODE_DIR="${MCP_CODE_DIR:-/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code}"`
- `:127-130` `code_repo_present()` — tests only `[ -e "${MCP_CODE_DIR}/.git" ]` and `git -C ... rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`
- `:155-159` `clone_code_locked()` rechecks presence and returns early: "code checkout was cloned by another container"
- `:162-164` clones only when absent/unusable
- `:175-177` `provision_code()` — `if code_repo_present; then return 0`

So on every normal restart and redeploy it exits immediately, leaving HEAD wherever it was.

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` never fast-forwards the volume:

- `:399-408` launches the MCP container with `MCP_CODE_DIR` / `REBAR_ROOT` pointed at the volume and mounts `gerrit_mcp_code:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`
- `:493-497` fetches only `/var/lib/rebar/mirror`
- `:557-575` no-op ticks do pressure cleanup, MCP self-heal, retire sweep, service checks — no workspace advance
- `:801-915` MCP redeploy rsyncs the mirror into the deploy repo and rebuilds the image, but only *mounts* the pre-existing volume
- `:951-959` success advances `$SHA_FILE` / `$MCP_SHA_FILE` marker files, not the code workspace

## Gates sign against it unknowingly

The completion close path is the serious one. It pins the default ref with `_pin_completion_ref(None)` -> `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` (`transition_close.py:128-143`), then `verify_with_auto_resume` calls `llm.verify_completion(..., source="attested", ref=(ref or "HEAD"), fetch=False, ...)` (`close_autoresume.py:271-279`). The post-verify signing drift check re-resolves *that same pinned SHA*, again without fetching (`transition_close.py:310-323`).

A stale-but-internally-consistent HEAD therefore passes the drift check and can emit a valid `completion-verifier` signature. The drift check compares the stale tree against itself, so staleness is invisible to it by construction.

Plan-review is partially protected but not authoritatively. `review_plan` and standalone `verify_completion` default to `origin/main` with `fetch=True`, so those producer paths can refresh before snapshotting. But claim-time currency is explicitly no-network: `current_head_sha` resolves the configured gate ref with `fetch=False` (`gate_source.py:89-109`), and scoped drift rehashing uses `gate_ref_hash_basis(..., fetch=False)`. Both compare against the *locally fetched idea* of `origin/main`, not the actual remote. The store-freshness machinery (`_store/freshness.py:109-169`) covers the ticket store only and never inspects `MCP_CODE_DIR`.

## Measured drift

Reflog on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` shows clone plus manual-only advances — no automated advance has ever occurred:

- clone at `f1dd41a8f0`, 2026-08-27 (539 commits behind current `origin/main`)
- manual `merge origin/main: Fast-forward` to `665d1d0480`, 2026-09-07 (135 behind current; was 130 behind at the recorded incident)
- manual fast-forwards on 2026-09-17 to `e5293bf5b1`, `e46d03aa83`, `5b143d9b15`, `4f12815e9a`, `71a719aef8`

Current HEAD `71a719aef8` matches local `origin/main` and the deploy markers — but only because of manual intervention, including mine earlier today.

## Implicated attestations, stated precisely

`f920-dc37-28e4-4a91` holds a valid `completion-verifier` signature at `verified-at-sha:e5293bf5b1...`, and `c65c-931c-ee39-4e63` one at `verified-at-sha:e46d03aa83...`. Ticket history records that the workspace had to be manually fast-forwarded to those SHAs before those closes could pass.

`f920` also carries a plan-review op-cert whose signed manifest anchors `verified-at-sha:5c2d3e664...` while the attestation plaintext `head_sha` reads `665d1d0480...`. `plan_review_status` now reports `stale-code` for it — but that verdict is computed from the locally available gate ref, not a remote fetch.

The distinction that matters: **the mechanism for a signed false PASS is demonstrated; an actual instance is not.** The observed `665d1d0480` incident produced a false FAIL, which is the safe direction. No attestation has been proven minted while the workspace was stale. A store-wide `verified-at-sha` census was attempted and cancelled for runtime, so that remains unestablished rather than ruled out.

## Fix direction

An operation-linked, in-process freshness boundary — not a GitHub-Actions-only trigger, which `project.portability` rejects. Shape: `fetch` + `merge --ff-only` on `MCP_CODE_DIR`, with dirty / diverged / unresolvable states failing loud and leaving the workspace untouched.

Wire it in both places, because they fail differently:

1. entrypoint / redeploy / no-op autodeploy tick — so drift cannot accumulate in the first place;
2. the gate path immediately before signing — so a stale workspace *refuses* rather than certifies.

(2) is the one that closes the correctness hole; (1) alone only shrinks the window. The gate check should report workspace HEAD, target SHA, and ahead/behind count, so a refusal is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

No changes were made. No AWS or Docker state was mutated. No LLM gate operation was run.
